claim: Aspect describes how an action is viewed, not when it happens.
note: Aspect is how the time of an event is viewed, not when it occurs; the Russian page defines вид as how the speaker conceives the course of the action in time.

claim: Imperfective can focus on an activity, repetition, or the fact that an action occurred without emphasizing its endpoint.
note: Activity/process and repetition/habit are stated. The clause 'the fact that an action occurred without emphasizing its endpoint' (general-factual use) is stated on neither page.

claim: The perfective focuses on accomplishing the action; the imperfective can describe the activity or its occurrence without that focus.
note: Perfective as a complete action and imperfective as process are stated. The imperfective describing an action's 'occurrence' without endpoint focus is not stated.

claim: An activity may have ended and still be described imperfectively when the focus is its process or occurrence rather than its endpoint.
note: Process focus is stated. That an activity which has ended can still be described imperfectively is not stated; the frozen example says the letters may still be unfinished.
